extracted.intended_audience: distance-education administrators, instructional designers, call-centre managers, and university leaders considering or operating call centres
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for designing, implementing, and managing call centres to support distance/online education, covering processes, technology, knowledge management, human resources, and change management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking student inquiries via CRM
rubrics_metrics.description: Track inquiries by course and whether they are related to administrative matters or academic content so faculty or instructional designers can mine them for issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRM tracking can identify instructional-design issues, subject-matter needing supplemental material or remedial exercises, and supports self-service help. It provides a systematic collection of information, avoids the 'recency effect,' and serves as a central collection point in distributed work environments. Use web-enabled tracking systems that produce reports and statistics for course improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call-centre consolidation / economies of scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidate call centres where similarities in tasks/services exist to achieve economies of scale and improved access to organizational information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation can reduce equipment costs, simplify technology implementation, improve control over service quality, reduce management requirements, and consolidate KM. Note research indicating subunit/team optimal size of ~50 agents — beyond which incremental gains are minimal. Consider consolidation of design, staff planning, standards reporting, IT liaison, contact automation, QA, and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segmentation strategy (routing by client value or student characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Segment routing not solely by agent skills but by client value/media or, in education, by student characteristics and query type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In business contexts low-value customers are routed to self-service and high-value to high-touch; for education, use segmentation by graduate vs undergraduate, area of study, or query type. Data from CRM should inform segmentation. Many queries can be routed to self-service while others go to specialized agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge management integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate organizational knowledge into systems so agents have services, corporate knowledge, and process flows needed to handle requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KM, process management, just-in-time training, and CRM tear down skills barriers so agents can handle diverse/difficult calls. As knowledge becomes incorporated into knowledge systems, training shifts to teaching relationship-building and process use. Integration increases consistency of messages and provides a 'single face' to customers/students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processes and policy development
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop, evaluate, and standardize processes and operational policies for call-centre operations and contact handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate types of contacts, routing, and contact-process management. Establish policies and standardized operational procedures and implement quality monitoring and reporting processes so the call centre meets established objectives. Use call-routing to allocate work and ensure relevant customer information is documented and accessible to agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy-first approach to technology (CRM/CEM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with a customer (student) strategy, realign structure and processes to fit that strategy, and then select appropriate technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid being dazzled by technology promises; CRM/CEM installations work best when technology follows strategy and processes. Choose mission-critical products driven by customer loyalty and service objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Experience Management (CEM) and metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify key measures for customer satisfaction and retention and gather statistics to guide call-centre operations and policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEM begins by determining measures for satisfaction/retention; its statistics help make sound operational decisions. Use gathered data to assess attitudes, brand perceptions, and responses to marketing; leverage contact data to unlock long-term loyalty and advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate technology selection and integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Select and integrate technology (VoIP, CRM, knowledge databases, multi-channel tools) that fit the institution’s strategy and customer-service goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate knowledge databases, CRM/customer tracking, CEM/follow-up, and handling of multiple contact media into accessible systems. Consider intelligent routing, web chat, email, voicemail, FAQs, and automated Q&A. Prioritize products that deliver mission-critical services and support customer loyalty objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-channel service design (web + phone support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide complementary multi-channel contact options (web, chat, email, phone, video) and ensure user interfaces make information quickly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Web-based tools (FAQs, intelligent Q&A, AskAU example) let customers find routine answers; channels should be complementary, not competitive. As routine issues move online, call centres must be prepared to handle more sophisticated calls and the overall 'service bar' rises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intelligent routing and matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Use automated systems to match customers with staff based on customer profile and staff knowledge focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intelligent routing directs calls (e.g., best customers to particular reps). Routing should consider client/student profile and staff expertise so calls go to individuals/automated agents best qualified to handle them, reducing referrals and call-backs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human resources: recruitment and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit front-line and call-centre managers with appropriate customer service skills, communication and writing skills, positive attitudes, experience, and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personnel costs are high; selection should ensure capability to provide quality services. Staff should be corporate ambassadors for the institution and possess the experience/education necessary to support students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training, coaching, and change involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide intensive, ongoing training and coaching, and involve staff in changes so they buy into new processes and have the information needed to carry them out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapidly changing technologies/processes require staff engagement and continual updates in policies/procedures. Groupware (call-back conferences) and collaborative tools can support staff in answering substantive queries or escalating appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and performance monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly assess employee satisfaction, customer feedback, retention, and service-standard compliance to inform improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use performance checks to monitor employee satisfaction and customer perceptions. Retention of staff is as important as retention of customers/students. Empowerment correlates with higher retention; monitor metrics to spot and correct issues quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-involvement HR practices to improve retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt high-commitment management techniques (increased CSR discretion, high task variety, reduced surveillance, team-oriented structures) to increase job satisfaction and retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher task variety, autonomy, and skill upgrading lead to higher employee satisfaction and productivity, thereby improving service quality and reducing absenteeism/turnover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role separation (one-window/tiered model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate administrative/tier-1 inquiries from academic/substantive queries and marking, using a one-window approach with Tier 1 advisors, academic experts, and specialist markers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 1 advisors (undergraduate student advisors) handle most administrative queries; academics focus on substantive academic issues; specialist markers handle marking. This separation increases efficiency, faster responses, reduces academics' administrative burden, and reduces costs (example: Athabasca University).

rubrics_metrics.name: Central tracking, assignment, and service-standard monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Use central databases and groupware to track queries, assign/reassign inquiries, monitor timeliness and compliance with service standards, and produce reports for course and operations improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A web-enabled comprehensive student tracking system should account for all queries (phone, email, call-back conference). Central posting of academic inquiries allows administrators to assign/reassign and monitor service standards, reducing litigation risks and addressing problem areas quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for disaster recovery and centralized operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralize operations such as centre design, staff planning, network design/management, standards reporting, IT liaison, contact automation, QA, and training to simplify disaster recovery and improve consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralization can simplify disaster-recovery planning, produce consistent messages, provide a single face to students, and enable economies of scale while widening services eligible for call-centre support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcoming cultural and academic resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame call-centre implementation to align with organizational culture and academics’ professional values, and demonstrate student- and institution-benefiting outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change must be presented as consistent with institutional values, not commercialization. Clarify what is and is not an academic inquiry so academics/tutors aren't threatened; highlight how elimination of tedious administrative inquiries can free academics for meaningful interactions and improve instructional quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting educational integrity and meaningful interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure call-centre use does not depersonalize learning; aim to increase meaningful academic interaction through better allocation of staff time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use savings from call-centre efficiencies to encourage course designs that increase meaningful student-academic interactions, thereby improving course value and countering criticisms that distance education is an industrialized, impersonal model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of call-centre for proactive student support and retention outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ call-centre staff for outbound retention/recruitment activities such as contacting students who are behind in coursework or potential applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance efficient outbound calling with customer focus. Use call-centre staff to support retention (e.g., contact students appearing behind to offer support) and, where appropriate, recruitment outreach while prioritizing customer-retention calls.
